observations.note: Luis Hernandez replaced Mickey Gall on two days notice
Gall withdrew with a medical issue; Luis Hernandez stepped in on two days notice

Coach Carlos Costa says the camp was built around Shevchenko for months - a full technical study, focused on takedown defence, timing entries and distance control - and the focus was changed completely when the UFC said she was out.
Promoted into a vacant-title main event after Shevchenko withdrew with a back and shoulder ligament injury. Reporting does not describe it as a short-notice booking.

First bout since December 2025, when he beat Cejudo. Says the inactivity was not injury: 'I've been waiting for the better part of a year. I've been spoken to about a bunch of fights, but I guess people have had better plans.'

UFC debut, and his first MMA bout since 20 February 2025 - about nineteen months. Describes himself as having been 'semi-retired' during the inactive spell in ONE. Had a professional boxing bout in September 2025.
Disclosed in an interview during this camp that the mother of his child has been diagnosed with leukemia.

Combat Press: Reynoso, a TUF alternate, was originally set to face fellow alternate Wushamo Hailai (DWCS Week 6, Sept 15); Tapology lists that bout cancelled after Hailai withdrew, reason not given. Rebooked against Bertolso two weeks later.
Sherdog lists her last fight as the LFA strawweight title win over Lany Silva at LFA 216 on 2025-09-05, so she has been out about 12.8 months.
Back down to featherweight: his last fight (CW 209, 2026-07-04) was at a 161 lb catchweight, where he weighed 160.7; about 12 weeks later he made 145.5 for tonight.

Cageside Press (2026-06-07): after beating Edmen Shahbazyan at UFC Vegas 118, Allen said he wants a title rematch with champion Sean Strickland and is open to Nassourdine Imavov or the Du Plessis-Usman winner. Said in June, before this bout was booked.
Cageside Press (2026-09-01): this is Duncan's first UFC main event, scheduled for five rounds; he comes in on a five-fight win streak that includes Jared Cannonier and Roman Dolidze.

MMA Sucka, relaying an MMA Junkie Radio interview: Camilo said he studied Herbert's loss to Ilia Topuria and that "Herbert sometimes struggles on the ground, and I see few spaces I can catch him striking, also."
Heavy.com, previewing this bout: Wellmaker "recently switched camps to American Top Team" after two straight UFC losses (GIDStats reported the move on 2026-05-29).

BoxingNews: Meerschaert, 38, moves up to light heavyweight for this fight after five straight losses at middleweight; he missed weight by 4 lb for his last fight (vs Jacob Malkoun, May 2026, held at a 190 lb catchweight per Cageside Press).
RotoWire, citing Marcel Dorff of Heavy: Artur Minev withdrew for an undisclosed reason and Prado now faces Ismael Bonfim, who steps in on short notice. No notice period is stated.
Heavy: Prado drops back to lightweight for this fight after three welterweight decision losses (Jake Matthews, Nikolay Veretennikov, Charles Radtke); no win since 2023.
RotoWire, citing Marcel Dorff of Heavy: Bonfim "steps in on short notice" to replace Artur Minev against Francisco Prado. The notice period is not stated.

Official weigh-ins 2026-10-09: Bonfim 163.5 lb, 7.5 lb over the 156 lb non-title lightweight limit; fined 25% of his purse; Bloody Elbow reports the bout goes ahead at a catchweight. Prado made weight (155). His third UFC weight miss.
Official weigh-ins 2026-10-09 (Cageside Press): Ribeiro 208.5 lb, 2.5 lb over the 206 lb non-title light heavyweight limit; fined 20% of his purse to Felipe Franco (205); the bout goes ahead.
Official weigh-ins 2026-10-09 (Cageside Press): Souza 117 lb, 1 lb over the 116 lb non-title strawweight limit; fined 20% of her purse to Loopy Godinez (115.5); the bout goes ahead.
Home of Fight interview (via EssentiallySports and MMASucka): Price says the UFC offered him one more fight he could not turn down and that this will be his last; he had retired in March 2026.
Heavy: Price returns from a brief retirement, announced in March 2026 after a first-round submission loss to Michael Chiesa at UFC Seattle, about six months before this bout; four straight losses.
RotoWire: Frye pulled out of his July 18, 2026 bout with Alvin Hines for undisclosed reasons; RJ Harris - his opponent here - replaced him on about a week's notice and won by first-round TKO.
AgentMMA's earlier preview listed Franco vs Alexander Poppeck for this card; current listings show Brendson Ribeiro. No named outlet reports why or when Poppeck left.

MMA Junkie (Nolan King), via Cageside Press: Blanchfield withdrew from this bout's original UFC 330 date (Aug 15) with an undisclosed injury - her first UFC withdrawal - and it moved to Edmonton. No report on her health since.
MMASucka (outlet framing, not her quote): Blanchfield wants a flyweight title shot against Valentina Shevchenko, and a win here would move her closer.
MMASucka: her bout with Blanchfield moved from UFC 330 (Aug 15) to Edmonton after Blanchfield's injury withdrawal - same opponent, about two months later, now in front of a Canadian crowd.
theScore and Low Kick MMA: Malott headlines in Canada for the third straight time (six of his eight UFC fights in Canada), on a four-fight win streak capped by a TKO of Gilbert Burns in April.
MMASucka: Buckley comes in on two straight decision losses (Kamaru Usman, Sean Brady) after six straight wins; outlets say his top-10 ranking is at stake.
Cageside Press (2026-08-10): Barriault is 1-5 in his last six fights.
Cageside Press (2026-08-11): UFC debut; he earned the contract on Dana White's Contender Series (Sept 2025, submission of Magno Dias) and has not fought since; four-fight win streak.

AgentMMA's booking story calls Nallo vs Landwehr a featherweight bout while event listings have it at lightweight - the weight class is not settled. Landwehr comes in on three straight losses (Dooho Choi, Morgan Charriere, Cub Swanson).
RotoWire: Diniz withdrew from a June 2026 bout with Jose Luiz 'Montanha' (UFC Vegas 119) with an undisclosed injury; nothing reported on his recovery.
RotoWire: his last fight was a second-round TKO loss to Mario Pinto on 2025-10-11 - about a year out of competition.
AgentMMA: Galanti (8-1) replaces Gilbert Urbina, who was ruled out, against Julien Leblanc in his UFC debut. The notice period is not stated.
AgentMMA: original opponent Gilbert Urbina was ruled out (no reason given); Leblanc now faces UFC newcomer Nick Galanti.
RotoWire, citing Marcel Dorff of Heavy: Louie Sutherland is out (listed injury, undisclosed); Mahjoub now faces UFC newcomer Joel Faglier.
RotoWire, citing Marcel Dorff of Heavy: Faglier replaces Louie Sutherland against Javad Mahjoub in his UFC debut. The notice period is not stated.
EssentiallySports: original opponent Jamey-Lyn Horth withdrew after a training injury and was not medically cleared after an MRI; Cerminara now faces Mackenzie Stiller.
Low Kick MMA: her first fight since a decision loss to Maycee Barber at UFC 299 (March 2024) - about two years and seven months out.
Low Kick MMA: she gave birth to her first child in August 2025; this is her first fight as a mother.
AgentMMA and EssentiallySports: Stiller replaces Jamey-Lyn Horth, who withdrew with a training injury, against Katlyn Cerminara in her UFC debut. No named outlet states the notice period.
Cageside Press interview (2026-10-01): nearly two years out since a decision loss to Cody Gibson (Nov 2024); he said the time went to rehab on a knee injury and that he kept training and sparring.
Cageside Press interview (2026-10-01): he calls this fight "kind of like a redemption story" after an unhappy last performance, also in Edmonton.
Heavy: his UFC debut comes more than a year after his Contender Series KO of Raphael Uchegbu (Sept 2025); no reason given for the gap.

Weigh-ins settle the weight class: Landwehr 155, Nallo 155.5 - a lightweight bout (156 non-title limit), Landwehr's first at 155. Sherdog and Hot Takes report the weights; all 26 fighters made weight.
Cageside Press, media day: three straight losses finally pushed him up from 145 to 155 - "Now, down three, man I've got nothing to lose." UFC.com ran the same story.
MiddleEasy: Robbie Lawler will corner him in Edmonton after about ten weeks of training at Kill Cliff FC.

Cageside Press: says he never gets over losses and must rein in his eagerness to finish after the first-round stoppage by Jai Herbert in his April UFC debut; MiddleEasy says he plans a more patient approach.
MMA Mania's live weigh-in report (via Yahoo): 186.5 on his first attempt, then made 186 - exactly the non-title limit - after stripping down behind a curtain. He made weight; no fine.
MiddleEasy: expects to dominate Barriault and says he will not get into a brawl, because long exchanges build Barriault's momentum.
Cageside Press: says he feels more pressure for this fight than for the White House card, where Bo Nickal stopped him in round 1.
Yahoo Sports weigh-in recap: one of the two scale scares - stripped down and weighed in behind a box, then made 136, exactly the non-title limit.
Cageside Press: at 36 he calls this the last chapter of his career and wants "good fights, good guys"; he comes in on a two-fight skid. MiddleEasy reported the same.
MiddleEasy: details his move to the Fight Sports gym, and says this is one of two fights left on his UFC contract.
MMA Mania: answering Buckley's popularity jibe, Malott said Buckley "would never headline in Canada without me"; at media day he told Cageside Press "this is my show" and called it a very good camp.
Cageside Press, media day: says Malott took the fight to raise his own profile - "You're trying to become the A-side"; this is Buckley's third UFC headliner.
Cageside Press, media day: calls it a title eliminator - "whoever wins this fight does expect a title shot"; Sherdog says she wants a title rematch with champion Natalia Silva in Toronto.
BJPenn.com: expects Blanchfield to turn to wrestling "once she feels these hands".
MiddleEasy, media day: the UFC has not promised her a title shot with a win; BJPenn.com says she expects a finish to earn one.
Cageside Press: UFC debut after the Contender Series; says he got the Nelson fight on about five or six weeks' notice and predicts a performance-of-the-night bonus.
Cageside Press: wants to "spoil the party" at Jourdain's debut and says he will out-class him if his game plan holds.
Yahoo News Canada: the Edmonton heavyweight finally gets a UFC fight in his hometown, at Rogers Place.
Cageside Press (2026-09-18): Arnold Allen is out of their UFC 333 bout; former Oktagon champion Losene Keita replaces him.
MMA Junkie via MMASucka: chose to stay on the card against the unranked Keita rather than wait for a ranked opponent - "sitting around and waiting for a ranked guy is not in my agenda."
Cageside Press (2026-09-18): replaces Arnold Allen against Aaron Pico about five weeks out, soon after his KO win at UFC Paris (2026-09-05).
Heavy: missed weight for his originally scheduled UFC debut (against Patricio Pitbull) before getting a second chance.
AgentMMA: before the booking, offered to fight any top-15 featherweight on short notice.
RotoWire (citing Heavy On Sports) lists him with an arm injury - a Paulo Costa high kick damaged his left arm in the TKO loss at UFC 327 (2026-04-11).
AgentMMA: Robert Whittaker said he broke Krylov's jaw in the round-3 TKO at UFC 329 (2026-07-11); another report said doctors found no fracture.
Newsweek (from 10 News): whether he retires depends on how UFC 333 goes - he would walk away after a bad beating; no plans to retire now.
The National (2026-10-06): "a nice long camp"; says his grappling prep with Craig Jones gives him confidence against an elite wrestler like Evloev.
PredictionHunt (2026-09-04): said on Sept 2 he cuts about 12 kg to make 145 lb and plans to move to lightweight after this fight.
MMA Junkie via MMASucka: says he will not chase a finish and wants to win over 25 minutes on the scorecards.
Low Kick MMA: nine-hour surgery on damaged lumbar discs after the UFC 323 title win (Dec 2025); in mid-June a teammate said he was about two months from training.
AgentMMA: back to pad work after back-surgery recovery; first fight since UFC 323 (2025-12-06).
AgentMMA: trilogy camp opened in Kislovodsk under Kairat Nurmaganbetov (partners incl. Kurban Gadzhiev, Asaf Chopurov), then moved to Dubai.
Yardbarker: added a new coach ('Jesse') for private sessions at Q MMA, Las Vegas, preparing for the Yan trilogy.
Heavy: lost to Henry Cejudo by technical fall in the RAF 12 freestyle wrestling main event (Aug 2026), during this fight's build-up.
